design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (Carver household; root = insured cancellation refund signed by the named insured). Rebuilt in rework round 2 against audits/policy_task/policy_endorsements_and_renewals/{_difficulty,0}.md.

0. Revision record (round 4, against the revision_3 sections of audits/policy_task/policy_endorsements_and_renewals/{_difficulty,0}.md).
- R3-P1 (financed window superseded one of three base sentences fixing the newly acquired window; base reading gave AP 151.84 / refund 365.28): the extended report window and its overwrite of auto_vehicle_changes are withdrawn. The charge-start ladder now tests the package's own newly_acquired_additional_report_days, exactly the window every base sentence states, so no base sentence is left in conflict. R2-O2 is closed by changing the row instead of the policy: the Kia addition (and its Ally loss payee entry) is now recorded 2026-09-12, day 11 of Basic's 14 days, so the acquisition-date effective date is what auto_vehicle_changes itself prescribes. Base and extended readings both give the charge from 2026-09-01.
- R3-F1 (financed_report_window rests on a condition the line does not weigh): the factor is removed. To keep the drawn four factors on the vehicle addition premium, the old two-source loyalty factor is split into its two business conditions: addition_loyalty_credit (tenure only: 60+ months 10 percent, 36-59 months 5 percent, otherwise nil) and continuous_coverage_share (parameter, the lapse marker: none -> whole credit; lapse 36+ months before booking -> half; more recent lapse -> none), the continuous-coverage condition carriers attach to tenure credits. Gold figures unchanged (183.41 / 103.73 / 378.46); every factor bears weight; the all-standard addition figure is now 218.14.

0''. Revision record (round 3, against the revision_2 sections of audits/policy_task/policy_endorsements_and_renewals/{_difficulty,0}.md).
- R2-F1 (minimum charge period billed 120 days with 101 left, past the 2027-01-01 expiration): the factor minimum_charge_period is withdrawn from the vehicle addition premium; charged days now never exceed the days left in the term. Its place is taken by financed_report_window (parameter): the newly acquired report window is the package's days, +30 where a new loan is recorded effective on the addition's effective date, +14 where a loan is recorded on another date, +0 for a cash purchase; the base window sentence of auto_vehicle_changes is declared overwritten.
- R2-O6 (tier 1 billed a prior-term addition again): an addition that took effect before the current term now charges nothing (charged days start at the term expiration date).
- R2-O2 / O7 (seeded Kia add keyed with its acquisition date though reported on day 21): with the Ally loan effective on the purchase date the Kia's window is 44 days, so the acquisition-date effective date is what the (overwritten) base window prescribes; the ladder order is now window-first (inside the window -> effective date; otherwise -> recorded date, which is the standard). R2-O1: lateness is measured from the addition's effective date in rule and compute alike.
- R2-P2 (loss payee notice: rule said the payoff was 'recorded', compute read its effective date): both notice ladders now speak only of when the payoff 'took effect (its effective date, whenever it was recorded)'; tier 2 now deducts the days from the credit start (removal) or cancellation date to a payoff that took effect after it, at most 10, so notice is never deducted for a lien that ended before the credit starts (also answers R2-O5's 'questionable' tier). The Kia payoff is reseeded effective 2026-10-01 (recorded 2026-10-02): 3 notice days under the only reading; the recorded-date figure is no longer admitted by the text. R2-O4: tier 1 now reads 'more new loans than loan payoffs are recorded', the netting compute does.
- R2-O3 (credit-base denominator not the AP's day basis): the removal credit divides the written charge by the days that charge was written for (from the effective date when reported inside the window, else from the recorded date), the same basis as the addition premium; here 122 days on both sides.
- R2-P1 (charter): the removal credit's sentence is now scoped: 'Where the removed vehicle was added during the current term with a premium effect, a vehicle removal credit is not booked until that addition carries its own additional premium entry on the policy.' Issue-time and prior-term additions (the Ranger here) are no longer blocked; they fall to the full-term-drop tier.
- Re-run: VA 180.41 -> 183.41, VR 94.27 -> 103.73, refund 381.16 -> 378.46; every factor bears weight; per-task and final gate blocks re-run.

0'. Revision record (round 2). Symptom -> root cause -> change -> re-run.
- G1 (removal-credit sentence weaker than its condition: a rental option's coverage_added entry already satisfied "its own coverage change entry"): the rental-option problem is withdrawn (G2a), and the new removal-credit sentence waits on "the removed vehicle's addition carries its own additional premium entry", a kind of entry the ordinary lifecycle writes only through the booking problem. Re-run: the sentence is false at the opening (no auto_additional_premium has the Kia addition as source).
- G2a/b/c (extended credits re-decided rental, physical damage and roadside premium, which their own charters return pro rata): the world is now liability-only (no physical damage, rental, roadside or DriveSense holdings), no extended rule earns or haircuts another product's premium, and the refund rule states that optional-coverage premium is returned pro rata and never cut by the return share.
- G3 (tenure_return_share labelled method): kept as a parameter; the honest method factor is cancellation_date_anchor (the request's date vs the signing day vs the term end).
- G4a (tenure/payment haircuts on endorsement credits) and G4b (DriveSense recapture): removed. The only billing-based tiers left are the cancellation charge and the plan-discount take-back on a whole-policy cancellation, which the audit did not flag.
- O2 (waiver condition wider in compute than rule): compute now requires no vehicle left AND every removal reason sold or total loss. O2b, O3: gone with the physical damage and rental reads. O4 (base no-backdating sentence): declared overwritten by the removal credit's credit-start ladder. O6 analogue: the removal credit carries the amount written on the addition's AP entry, not an existence switch. O-T0-3: the inventory below is recounted.

1. Why this is a good test. Denise, already moved to Florida, asks only to finish the cancellation she started online (request awaiting signature, dated 2026-10-03) and to learn the refund. The refund rule says "The cancellation refund is fixed only after every vehicle removal recorded on the policy during the term carries its own return premium entry." The ledger shows the Kia Soul's removal (sold 2026-09-28, recorded 2026-10-02) with no return premium entry. The removal-credit rule says "Where the removed vehicle was added during the current term with a premium effect, a vehicle removal credit is not booked until that addition carries its own additional premium entry on the policy." The Kia's addition (acquired 2026-09-01, recorded 2026-09-12) has none either. The agent must find both hops from the records, book the addition premium, then the removal credit, then hand Denise the signature with the right date and refund.

2. Scope. Draw: prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[5, 5, 4]. Claimed: auto_ext_insured_cancellation_refund (5 factors, owner=user sign_cancellation_request_695fb1aa), auto_ext_vehicle_removal_credit (5, book_vehicle_removal_credit_524db3a4), auto_ext_vehicle_addition_premium (4, book_vehicle_addition_premium_9393c661). Task 1 holds the driver addition premium and the exclusion credit; scopes disjoint.

3. Problem-tree card. Chain: refund <- removal credit <- addition premium.
Edge 1 (refund <- removal credit): value_input, gate cx_written, state form, affirmative "only after". False at opening: initial_state.auto_transactions.<Kia removal>.premium_effect = return and no RP has it as source. Only book_vehicle_removal_credit ties a return premium entry to a removal (the refund's own RP has no source; the exclusion RP sources an exclusion). Skip run: refund 421.78 instead of 378.46.
Edge 2 (removal credit <- addition premium): value_input, gate vr_written, state form, negated "not ... until". False at opening: the Kia addition (premium_effect additional, effective 2026-09-01 inside the term) has no AP with it as source. Only book_vehicle_addition_premium ties an AP to a vehicle addition. Skip run: removal credit 0.00 (credit base nil: nothing charged) instead of 103.73, refund 345.19.
Order: addition premium (step 8) -> removal credit (step 10) -> signature (step 14). The customer's own write is the root (only the named insured can sign a cancellation; lifecycle in_force -> cancelled by user). Persona names no prerequisite; tools validate none.

4. Base-invariant card. Refund (auto_insured_cancel + auto_return_premium): auto_insured_cancellation's signed-request gate declared overwritten (signature carries out the cancellation); "takes effect on the date the named insured chose ... never an earlier one" kept and implemented by cancellation_date_anchor (request 2026-10-03 < signing 2026-10-05 -> 2026-10-05); fee and minimum earned premium waived only when no vehicle is left and every removal was a sale or total loss (2 vehicles left: not waived); cap written premium less minimum earned premium (856.38, not binding); never below zero. Pro rata clauses of auto_insured_cancellation and auto_evt_midterm_proration declared overwritten (90 percent short-rate standard, full pro rata for 60+ months without lapse; optional coverages always pro rata). Removal credit and addition premium (auto_return_premium / auto_additional_premium): no subject-scoped gate; the base day-count clause and the no-backdating clause are declared overwritten; the newly acquired report window is the base's own (Basic 14 days) and drives late_report_charge_start, the Kia being reported on day 11.

5. Business-object card. Kia addition 2f74b055 (only vehicle addition with a premium effect); Kia removal 8e9dd7f8 (only removal); AP/RP entries tie by source_transaction_id. Loss payee entries: Camry new loan (Fifth Third, 2021) still open; Kia new loan (Ally, effective 2026-09-01) and payoff effective 2026-10-01 (recorded 2026-10-02), three days after the sale. Written premium of the 2026-07-01 term: 826.70 term premium plus the entries written in-call; the 2021 replacement AP (term 2021-01-01) and the 2026-01-01 term premium are excluded by term.

6. Factor card (handling time; figure = result with only that factor at its standard).
Addition premium 183.41 (all-standard 218.14): late_report_charge_start (method) recorded on day 11 of 14 -> from 2026-09-01 [166.88]; excess_vehicle_rating (parameter, multi-source) 3 vehicles vs 2 drivers -> 85% [215.78]; addition_loyalty_credit (parameter) 99 months -> 10% [203.79]; continuous_coverage_share (parameter) no lapse marker -> whole credit [203.79].
Removal credit 103.73 (all-standard 178.83): deletion_credit_basis (method) AP 183.41 written -> unearned share x 92/122 [135.60]; deletion_credit_start (method) recorded 4 days later, within allowance -> 2026-09-28 [102.60]; deletion_backdating_allowance (parameter) sale -> 30 days [102.60]; loss_payee_notice (parameter) payoff took effect 2026-10-01, 3 days after the credit start -> 3 days [107.11]; short_hold_share (parameter) 27 days -> 0.75 [138.31].
Refund 378.46 (all-standard 349.00): cancellation_date_anchor (method) -> 2026-10-05 [388.17]; cancellation_loss_payee_notice (parameter) 2 new loans vs 1 payoff (Camry open) -> 10 days [426.98]; tenure_return_share (parameter, multi-source) 99 months no lapse -> 100% [340.62]; plan_discount_takeback (parameter, cross billing) EFT 3% -> 1.5% [384.23]; payment_method_charge (parameter, multi-source, cross billing) autopay, no return in 12 months (2025-08-04 return is 14 months back) -> 0 [328.46].
Near-misses: the 2025-08 returned payment outside the window; the Kia's payoff (closes its loan, recorded a day after it took effect) vs the Camry's open loan; replacement entry not counted as a vehicle add; prior-term APs excluded by term.

7. Seed rows (32): 1 customer, 2 drivers, 4 vehicles (Ranger, Malibu replaced 2021, Camry, Kia), 1 policy, 14 auto transactions (2 vehicle adds and 2 driver adds at issue, Camry replacement + its AP, Camry new loan, 2026-01-01 term premium, renewal offer, 2026-07-01 term premium, Kia addition without AP, Kia new loan, Kia payoff, Kia removal without RP), 1 change request, 1 billing account, 8 billing ledger rows. No physical damage, rental, roadside, telematics or filing rows: nothing of another product's premium is on GT's path.

8. Persona. Denise, friendly, already in Sarasota; volunteers only the goal; phone and ZIP when asked; the Kia, the loans (payoff went through October 1) and autopay only on direct questions; accepts a later date than the one on the form; one passive, conditional consent with no ordering word; signs with the reference, date and amount given.

9. Standard solution: 0-1 locate/verify; 2-6 read policy, vehicles, drivers, request, ledger; 7-8 book the Kia addition premium 183.41; 9-10 book the Kia removal credit 103.73; 11-12 read billing account and ledger; 13-14 hand over, Denise signs (request, 2026-10-05, 378.46).

10. Verification: harness on check_compute's evaluator gives 183.41 / 103.73 / 378.46; skip runs 0.00 (removal without addition premium), 421.78 (refund without removal credit), 345.19 (refund without addition premium). Per-task gates: EXTENDED, TASK TOOL CONTRACT, REPLAY (closure 32 = initial 32), SOLVABILITY, COMPUTE, GROUNDING, SCOPE all OK.
user_scenario:
You are Denise Carver, 55, a retired school librarian, calling Cardinal Mutual on a Monday morning from your new kitchen in Sarasota, Florida, where you and your husband Mark arrived on October 2 to live near your daughter. Your Florida car insurance with another company started on October 3. That same day you went into the Cardinal website and started cancelling your Ohio auto policy, putting October 3 as the date, but the site said a signature was still needed and you never finished. You want the cancellation done on this call, as early as Cardinal will allow, and you want to know what Cardinal will give back. You will sign the cancellation yourself when the representative hands it to you. You are not asking for anything else today.

You open by saying, in your own friendly way, that you've moved to Florida and want to finish cancelling your Cardinal car insurance. When they ask for your phone number you give 6145550104; when they ask for your ZIP code you give 43212, the Columbus ZIP still on your account. Only if they ask for more do you give your date of birth, March 9, 1971 (1971-03-09), the last four of your driver's license, 2417, or your email, denise.carver71@gmail.com. If they ask which policy, it is policy number CAP-OH-5531207, the only Cardinal auto policy you have. If they ask about the date, you put October 3 on the form because that is when the Florida policy started, and you understand if it has to be a little later.

Other questions you answer plainly from memory, without volunteering more. If they ask which cars are on the policy, you say the Ford Ranger and the Toyota Camry, which still has a loan with Fifth Third. If they ask about any other car, you say Mark bought a used Kia Soul at the start of September, on a loan from Ally, and sold it on September 28 when you decided two cars were enough for Florida; the buyer's payoff of the Ally loan went through on October 1. If they ask how you pay, the premium comes out of your checking account automatically every month. You don't know how Cardinal works out a refund and you won't guess at any number.

If the representative tells you something else on the policy needs handling as part of this, you say that's fine, go ahead. When they tell you the cancellation date and the refund and hand you the cancellation to sign, you sign it using exactly the request reference, the date and the refund amount they give you, and you read back what the signing shows. Once it shows the policy is cancelled, you thank them, say you'll watch for the refund, and say goodbye. If instead they tell you it cannot be finished today, you ask them once to explain why, then thank them and end the call.

edges.condition: The removed vehicle having been added during the current term with a premium effect, the policy's transaction history carries, in the current term, an additional premium entry whose source is that addition entry.
edges.policy_source: Where the removed vehicle was added during the current term with a premium effect, a vehicle removal credit is not booked until that addition carries its own additional premium entry on the policy.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A chain: the refund 'is fixed only after' the removal carries its return premium entry, and the removal credit 'is not booked until' the removed vehicle's addition carries its additional premium entry; no problem has two prerequisites, so no pair of writes can be reordered.
